title: Water and Society – Institutional Capacity Building in Water Management and Climate Change adaptation in selected countries in Asia (WaSo-Asia)
body: Water challenges are locally specific, but many underlying questions, governance, adaptation, capacity and community needs are shared. International collaboration is most valuable when it does not simply transfer solutions, but creates opportunities to learn from different contexts.

title: Remote Sensing Technology in River Basin Management
summary: JAXA / University of Tokyo /ADB Technical AssistanceBangladesh Water Dev. Board,2009 – 2014
body: Between 2009 and 2014, Dr. Rahman served as Country PI on two projects that paired Japan's space agency (JAXA) and the University of Tokyo with Bangladesh Water Development Board using satellite remote sensing to strengthen river basin management and build an early warning system for water disasters

title: Strengthening Environmental & Social Framework (ESF) Capacity in Bangladesh and Bhutan-funded by the World Bank
summary: Building a Sustainable Learning Center at BUET.
body: Under the leadership of Prof. Dr. Md. Mafizur Rahman, the World Bank-funded project Strengthening Environmental & Social Framework (ESF) Capacity in Bangladesh and Bhutan established a standardized institutional, digital, and curricular engine that transformed isolated training workshops into a scalable, self-sustaining public sector safeguard learning hub.Initiated through the 2022 World Bank negotiations, the project established institutional governance, dedicated facilities, and a custom Moodle digital learning system backed by standardized operating protocols. Under Dr. Rahman's direction, the team authored contextualized ESF, OHS, GEMS, and bidding manuals, validating the curriculum through 2023 pilot professional courses and built-in feedback loops. This foundational infrastructure enabled seamless scaling across multi-batch technical workshops and self-sustaining nationwide initiatives, including the 61-district LGED training program.

title: Agrometeorological data analysis and future scenario development of 487 Upazilas in Bangladesh
summary: World Bank / Bangladesh Weather& Climate Services RegionalProgram (BWCSRP),DAE,2018 – 2020
body: A single national climate policy cannot solve regional micro-climate challenges. Every Upazila has a different soil profile, a different cropping calendar, a different exposure to drought, salinity, or flash flooding. A national climate adaptation policy that treats them as interchangeable will fail most of them.A farmer in the northern drought-prone belt faces fundamentally different risks than a community in the coastal saline zone. To build true climate resilience, engineering and policy must meet at the intersection of Data Granularity,Agrometeorological Actionability and Inter-Agency Integration. As we face accelerating environmental shifts, the future of civil and environmental engineering relies heavily on combining spatial intelligence (GIS/Remote Sensing) with grassroots climate data.  How is your sector adapting macro-level climate data for localized execution.
